mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 7% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of triggered months at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.5% for three consecutive months, accompanied by accelerating payroll growth (PAYEMS > 200k monthly for three months), signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and cost-push inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.5% for 3 months AND PAYEMS > 200000 for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from the baseline at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% during a recession (UNRATE > 7%) signals a policy-driven monetary easing that lowers risk-free rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 65% of triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above 10% YoY for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent deceleration in both industrial production (INDPRO) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 0.3% month-over-month signals a synchronized slowdown in supply and demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for four consecutive months, with no corresponding decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL flat or falling), signals deteriorating labor market conditions without offsetting cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.5% for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL MoM <= 0
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes at 95% confidence.
